notes.title: Game Flow and Phases
notes.notes:
Greetings rangers,

As the first playtest draws near, let’s take a moment and get into how games progress in Galaxy Tactics.

Each game is composed of a number of rounds, which play out until one of the teams is declared victorious. In turn, every round is composed of 3 phases:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45538476/ec85ee136ebd4401ceb0b59ebc863abebc9a6d9f.png[/img]

[h1]1. Move and Fire[/h1]
This phase takes the first 10 seconds of every round. During this time, players may move by walking or using their jetpacks for the first 8 seconds. Also during this phase, players can select a weapon, aim and lock in (fire).

In this phase players usually move around the map to get into a better firing position, take cover from possible enemy attacks, or get out of a perilous situation.

[h1]2. Fire Only[/h1]
After the Move and Fire phase has ended, the Fire Only phase begins, where players can only select weapons, aim and lock in (fire). This phase can last a maximum of 20 seconds, but will end early once all players have either locked in or skipped.

It is highly recommended that teammates coordinate their shots, and check what weapons their allies will use based on the icons above the health bars. Players may also use the targeting feature to indicate where they intend to fire.

In both the Move and Fire and Fire Only phases, if a player does not wish to fire, they can simply skip the round.

[h1]3. Action[/h1]
Once the Fire Only phase ends, the Action phase begins, and all locked in weapons are fired. This phase lasts until there is no more movement (action) on the map. In case of unexpected events which would keep the Action phase alive, it will end forcefully after 25 seconds.

After the Action phase ends, and after a brief pause, a new round begins with the Move and Fire phase.

[h3]Nuke[/h3]
If a game reaches 15 minutes, a Nuke will be triggered which deals damage to all players each round, forcing the game to come to an end after a few rounds.

[h3]Draws[/h3]
One of the teams is declared victorious once all opponents are eliminated. As draws are not allowed in Galaxy Tactics, if the last players on both teams are eliminated in the same round, a winner is declared based on total team damage or weapons accuracy.

[h3]Got questions?[/h3]
If you need more details, just ask here on Steam or join Galaxy Tactics on Discord!

notes.title: Playtest Weekend
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45538476/9e4c445d935e6c2d8dfd00ffc6c49cc91761a930.jpg[/img]

Hey everyone,

I'm happy to invite you to the first Galaxy Tactics playtest weekend. The playtest will begin on April 19th, and if you would like to try out the game, you can sign up on Steam right now.

Start time: [b]Saturday April 19th, 8am UTC[/b] (1am L.A.  |  4am N.Y.  |  10:00 Paris  |  17:00 Tokyo)
Duration: 48 hours

[b]Playtest goals:[/b]
[list]
[*] Gameplay - how do you feel about the overall gameplay experience?
[*] Balance - do you feel that a weapon is too weak/powerful?
[*] Bugs - did you encounter any bugs or issues with the game?
[*] Server (this one's for me) - check if the server side runs as expected
[/list]

[b]Content[/b]
With a few exceptions, all content is available in this playtest:
[list]
[*] Campaigns and emotes are in development and not available
[*] Offline play is not available in playtests
[/list]

[b]Progress saved[/b]
Excluding any dramatic developments, all your progress in this and future playtests should be preserved if you will buy the game after launch.

[b]Discord[/b]
You can [url=https://galaxytactics.com/redirect/discord.html]join the Discord server here[/url] to chat and share your feedback.


See you on the battlefield!
